record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.context_brief: Recurrence of powers of recurrent sequences
record.original_question: Suppose an integer sequence a(n) is good for ℓ-recurrence of powers, meaning that for every nonzero integers k1, ..., kℓ and every measure-preserving transformation T, some n gives positive measure to A ∩ T^{k1 a(n)}A ∩ ... ∩ T^{kℓ a(n)}A whenever μ(A) > 0. Does it follow that each power sequence a(n)^k is good for ordinary 1-recurrence for every k = 1, ..., ℓ?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. If (a(n)) is good for `-recurrence of powers, is then (a(n)^k) good for 1-recurrence for k = 1, . . . , `?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell \geq 1$ be an integer. An integer sequence $(a(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is called good for $\ell$-recurrence of powers if for every invertible measure-preserving transformation $T$ of a probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$, every measurable set $A\subseteq X$ with $\mu(A)>0$, and every nonzero integers $k_1,\dots,k_\ell$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T^{k_1 a(n)}A\cap T^{k_2 a(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T^{k_\ell a(n)}A\bigr)>0.$$
A sequence $(b(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is called good for $1$-recurrence if for every invertible measure-preserving transformation $T$ on a probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ and every measurable $A$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n$ with $\mu(A\cap T^{b(n)}A)>0$.

Question: If $(a(n))$ is good for $\ell$-recurrence of powers, does it follow that for each $k=1,2,\dots,\ell$ the sequence $(a(n)^k)$ is good for $1$-recurrence?
